chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr said: Ibn Najjashi asked: Who is the Imam after your companion?
I went to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) and informed him. He said: The Imam after me is my son? Then he said: Can anyone who does not have a son dare to say: 'My son'?

key_terms.صَاحِبُكُمْ: Your companion (referring to the previous Imam)

ai.seo_question: Who is the Imam after Imam al-Sadiq according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the Imam’s precise linguistic logic in establishing hereditary succession (*Nass*), specifically addressing the potential ambiguity of the phrase 'my son' if the speaker were childless. It underscores the Shia doctrine of *Nass* (explicit designation) by linking the title of Imam directly to biological lineage, a key criterion distinguishing the Ahl al-Bayt from other claimants. The rhetorical question serves to validate the Imam’s paternity as a necessary condition for the validity of his designation.
